lessons: The guide calls WR the best pair by games, and I went 2-1 with it, but my games ran 14 to 26 turns, not the 9 to 17 fast-start pattern, so plan for grinds.
The guide says skip Riot Devils unless red is deep, yet I took two in pack 2 and pack 3 and played one, which was a wasted pick I would change for a removal spell or flier.
The guide says 16 lands is worth trying for low-curve aggro, but my 17-land WR lost 1-2 to RG in 14, 21 and 26 turns, so test 16 lands.
Round 1's WR deck ran two Smite the Monstrous, which hits power 4+; my Skaab Goliath and Galvanic Juggernaut were liabilities against it, so value cheap threats in UB tempo.
Victim of Night cannot target Vampires, Werewolves or Zombies; since it was my main removal, check opposing creature types before counting it as an answer.
My games ran 18 to 26 turns even with a low curve, so the deck lacked early pressure; take two-drops and early evasive creatures over late filler like Think Twice.
Where tonight contradicted the guide, fliers did not win: my UB Stitched Drake, Moon Heron and Battleground Geist lost to Somberwald Spider reach and Victim of Night, so count reach and removal.
Stop taking Bloodcrazed Neonate, Cellar Door, Dream Twist and Memory's Journey: all four were cut, so take a playable two-drop or Blazing Torch-level removal instead.
My games ran 11 to 26 turns, so take cheap threats over situational spells and draft for early pressure rather than waiting to stabilise against WU and UB.
Take the bomb and stay in its colour: my first-pick Olivia Voldaren went unplayed in my WU deck, which then ground through 19–25 turn games and lost matches.
My WU deck's interaction, including Rebuke and Lost in the Mist, kept games going for 19–25 turns without closing them out, so draft evasive threats over extra removal.
Take the third flier over Silverchase Fox or Unruly Mob: my WR took both, ran only Abbey Griffin and Midnight Haunting as fliers, and lost 1-2 to RG in a 27-turn game.
The guide says cheap starts win in 9 to 17 turns, but tonight's games ran 13 to 27 turns, so cheap creatures needed late fliers or Rally the Peasants to close.
The guide says to skip Kessig Wolf, yet my WR main-decked it, so cut it for a flier or removal spell.
Garruk Relentless plus Dead Weight, Prey Upon, Tribute to Hunger and Morkrut Banshee carried BG to 2-0 wins over BR and UB, so take cheap removal over mid-curve creatures early.
BG lost round 1 1-2 to WR in 20 to 22 turn games, likely because its grindy top end was too slow against early pressure like Silverchase Fox, so prioritize early blockers and two-drops.
Three Darkthicket Wolves and Spider Spawning were dependable, but Brain Weevil and Hamlet Captain were cut for early board presence, so draft more cheap creatures rather than extra top end.

The guide's 'BR vampires are aggressive' plan failed: my ground creatures stalled against green decks, with games running 17-30 turns, so prioritize fliers and reach over filler 2-drops like Walking Corpse.
Round 1 and 2 losses came against green bodies like Boneyard Wurm and Somberwald Spider, so draft cheap removal such as Dead Weight, Victim of Night, or Tribute to Hunger early.
Stay flexible: a 0-3 record with 1-6 games shows my creature-heavy BR curve lacked evasion; take fliers like Stitched Drake or Chapel Geist over a third Crossway Vampire.

Green-red fight and burn removal carried this RG deck to 3-0 in matches: take Prey Upon, Brimstone Volley, Geistflame, and Into the Maw of Hell early, then fill the 2-3 drop slots with green creatures.
Two WR opponents ran Smite the Monstrous, which kills four-power creatures like Boneyard Wurm, so prefer cheaper creatures over a second Boneyard Wurm when facing WR.
Don't spend early picks on marginal spells like Make a Wish or Grimoire of the Dead; take playable creatures and real answers like Bramblecrush, which my deck needed more.
